title: A reply after its asker gave up is receipted
intention: A reply that lands after its asker's request() gave up is receipted by the bus as given up, so it no longer stands undelivered for report_stood to raise as stood mail. In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py: BusDevice holds _abandoned, a dict from request id to asker. When request() reaches its deadline it records the id there, takes a reply that landed in the ring meanwhile, and otherwise raises TimeoutError as before. post() pops reply_to from _abandoned. For a personal reply with no delivery hook and no folder receiver, it records the receipt by='bus-asker-gave-up'.
why: Law 7: the stood trouble names the wrong failure. The mail did reach its addressee's door; the asker had stopped waiting. A receipt naming that is the true record. Measured 2026-10-18 by CC: 5 of 6 standing envelopes were tester->constrain 'run' replies that landed 3-13 min after constrain's 180s timeout (cairn/devices/codemother/machines/constrain/constrain.py:371). Law 1: the same 39-count trouble re-raises on every flush.

falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_reply_after_its_asker_gave_up_is_receipted.py exits 0. (1) A request() to a silent addressee times out, its reply posted afterwards is not in undelivered(to=<asker>) after flush. (2) That reply's one delivery row has by='bus-asker-gave-up'. (3) A reply to an envelope that was never a request stays undelivered. Measured 2026-10-18: teeth 1 and 2 red against today's bus.py, all three green with the change. Horizon: PROVED, with the hollow revert of cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py redding teeth 1 and 2; after it, the standing constrain replies drain once and mail-constrain-stood-600s clears.
watchme: none, because the outcome is a late reply receipted as given up, checked by cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_reply_after_its_asker_gave_up_is_receipted.py, which reruns at every reseal touching the bus; a recurrence shows as stood mail raised by report_stood in cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py

decisions.text:
D1 (the /sorted builder_check): Questions a Haiku builder would need, answered. (a) The one file that changes is cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py: _abandoned in __init__; gave_up popped at the top of post()'s personal branch, and an elif receipting it by='bus-asker-gave-up' after the folder branch; request() records the id and checks the ring once before raising. (b) The exact change is this unified diff, applied verbatim with git apply:
diff --git a/cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py b/cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py
index 838234e8..432fea15 100644
--- a/cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py
+++ b/cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/bus.py
@@ -204,6 +204,10 @@ class BusDevice(BaseDevice):
         # Ids of requests whose asker is inside ``request()`` right now: a bounce answering one
         # is the asker's to take by correlation, never the no-receiver path's (ticket 7cb1989e7825).
         self._asked: set[str] = set()
+        # Ids of requests whose asker's ``request()`` reached its deadline, keyed to that asker
+        # (ticket cd2d27fe3261): a reply landing later has nobody to take it, so the bus
+        # receipts it as given up rather than let it stand for report_stood to raise.
+        self._abandoned: dict[str, str] = {}
         self._channel_toggles: dict[str, dict[str, bool]] = {}
         self._ring: list[dict] = []
         self._ring_receipts: list[dict] = []
@@ -456,6 +460,7 @@ class BusDevice(BaseDevice):
             "sender": sender, "addressee": to, "channel": channel,
         })
         if channel == "personal":
+            gave_up = self._abandoned.pop(reply_to, None) if reply_to is not None else None
             hook = self._delivery_hooks.get(to)
             toggles = self._channel_toggles.get(to, {})
             if hook is not None and toggles.get(channel, True):
@@ -467,6 +472,8 @@ class BusDevice(BaseDevice):
                     })
             elif self._try_folder_delivery(to, envelope):
                 pass
+            elif gave_up is not None:
+                self.record_delivery(envelope["id"], to=to, by="bus-asker-gave-up")
             elif (hook is None and self._no_receiver is not None
                   and (reply_to is None or (envelope["body"].get("is_bounce")
                                             and reply_to not in self._asked))):
@@ -587,6 +594,10 @@ class BusDevice(BaseDevice):
                     return self._taken(replies[0], sender)
         finally:
             self._asked.discard(envelope["id"])
+        self._abandoned[envelope["id"]] = sender
+        late = self._ring_matches(reply_to=envelope["id"])
+        if late and self._abandoned.pop(envelope["id"], None) is not None:
+            return self._taken(late[0], sender)
         raise TimeoutError(
             f"no reply to envelope {envelope['id'][:8]}… from {to} "
             f"within {timeout}s — the target did not reply (CP1: loud, not empty)"

(c) The proof cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_reply_after_its_asker_gave_up_is_receipted.py is committed red-first, and the builder edits nothing there. (d) Run bin/cairn test cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/test_a_reply_after_its_asker_gave_up_is_receipted.py and expect 3 green, then test_a_requester_takes_its_reply.py, test_bus.py, test_delivery.py and test_exchange.py in the same proofs folder, all green.
